title: runtime pocket notebook — iris
content:
Morning brain dump (quick, unpolished)

Context: oncall handoff from Kai. Focus today = triage lingering p99 spikes + small kernel changes to KV cache eviction heuristics. Quick notes to self and commands that actually matter.

Goals for the day:
- Short-term: kill the evening p99 regression seen on small-req workloads (RI-4723)
- Med-term: prototype a light-weight eviction heuristic that prefers contiguous KV ranges
- Admin: add a basic smoke test that reproduces the spike locally under ~100 concurrent tiny requests

Immediate triage checklist:
- Reproduce on dev: use loadscript-small-reqs.py with --seq-len 64 --qps 150
  - local cmd: python tools/loadscript-small-reqs.py --host http://localhost:8080 --concurrency 96 --seq-len 64 --duration 120
- Confirm whether p99 correlates with cache misses or GPU kernel queuing
  - metrics: serve.kv.cache.hit_rate, serve.gpu.queue_length, runtime.kernel.sch_latency
- Quick logging hack: add temporary tagged logs at kv_cache->evict() entry/exit (tag: iris-debug-evict)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Small requests create many short-lived KV entries, eviction runs during bursts and triggers a stall while copying ranges (eviction lock + memcpy)
2) Batching heuristic in scheduler conflates tiny seqs, grows batch latency due to per-request serialization on server side
3) Memory fragmentation on host-side allocator causes malloc slow-path under burst allocations (rare but possible)

Quick experiments to run (fast wins first):
- Experiment A: flip eviction to background thread with softer mutex (try std::shared_mutex read-lock for lookups, exclusive for eviction)
  - File: runtime/kv/cache_manager.cc (annotate with TODO: background-evict proof-of-concept)
- Experiment B: instrument per-request KV lifetime and log percentiles (store small histogram, emit once every 10s)
- Experiment C: force-use of contiguous page allocator for test build (set ENV USE_CONTIG_ALLOC=1)

Commands & snippets I keep forgetting:
- Build dev image (fast) : ./scripts/build.sh -j8 --target=dev-runtime
- Run tiny-load locally: docker run --rm -it -p 8080:8080 dev-runtime:local /bin/bash -c "/opt/runtime/bin/serve --config conf/local.yaml"
- Grep logs for debug-tag: rg "iris-debug-evict" -n logs/ | tail -n 200

Notes to self while pairing later:
- When adding background eviction be wary of ordering with KV cache migration (we move hot prefixes between partitions)
- Avoid touching KVCache::lookup signature; add wrapper for instrumentation instead
- Add feature flag: runtime.kv.eviction.mode=background|inline for quick toggles in prod (default inline for now)

Unresolved questions to bring to design sync:
- Do we allow eviction to copy data while lookups happen, or must it always hold a snapshot? (consistency tradeoff)
- If background eviction wins, what's the impact on CPU budget for dedicated nodes? Need a rough budget calc: ~1-2 cores per 8 GPUs?

Quick test plan (manual):
- Baseline: current master -> run loadscript, record p50/p95/p99, hit_rate, queue_len for 3 runs of 2m
- Patch A (background-evict): same runs, compare metrics. Look for >20% p99 drop without hit_rate regression
- Patch B (contig alloc): same runs, check if kernel latency tail changes

To-dos (micro):
- [ ] Add logging tags and re-run CI perf job locally (priority: high)
- [ ] Open a short RFC if background eviction shows >15% improvement (target: this week)
- [ ] Add smoke test script to tools/ci/smoke-kv-spike.sh
- [ ] Annotate PR with performance numbers and a brief explanation of why background eviction is safe

Misc notes / brain fragments:
- Saw a trace with long memcpy in evict path at 02:17 UTC (trace id: trace-9d3f). Save that trace as evidence to link to PR.
- Slack thread: #runtime-debug — post quick summary and invite Kai and Asha for pairing at 13:30 PT.
- If time: re-check scheduler's batching window (default 5ms) — maybe reduce to 3ms for tiny-req workloads, but that could hurt throughput

End-of-day quick handoff (what I'll push before leaving):
- Push debug logging PR for quick revertability
- Upload perf runs to tmp/iris/ri-4723/
- Leave a note in #runtime-debug with a short summary + where to find runs

Notes to future me: write smaller commits, make rollback trivial, and mark everything experimental with feature flags.

-- Iris
